chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who enters into Ihram while wearing a shirt: He said, 'He should remove it without tearing it; and if he wore it after entering Ihram, he should tear it and remove it from what is below his legs.'

key_terms.إحرام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.مما يلي رجلَيْه: From what is below his legs

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on removing a shirt worn during Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'qabd' (covering the body) by distinguishing between garments worn before Ihram, which must be removed without tearing, and those put on after, which are torn to avoid the penalty of wearing stitched clothing. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on minimizing damage to the garment while strictly adhering to the prohibition of stitched attire for men. The ruling underscores the practical application of the Ihram restrictions during the sacred state of pilgrimage.
